problem: Typo in the last commit message (not pushed)
notes: Only for commits nobody else has. After a push use a follow-up commit instead.

problem: Forgot to add a file to the last commit (not pushed)
alternative: Commit it separately as fix: or chore:
notes: Check git status first so --amend doesn't pull in unrelated staged changes.

problem: Undo the last commit but keep the changes (not pushed)
alternative: git reset --mixed HEAD~1 to also unstage
notes: Changes stay in the working tree. Nothing is lost.

problem: Undo the last commit and throw the changes away (not pushed)
safest_fix: git branch backup/before-reset && git reset --hard HEAD~1
notes: reset --hard deletes uncommitted work too. Backup branch first; reflog can still find the commit for about 90 days.

problem: Undo a commit that is already pushed or shared
alternative: git revert -m 1 <merge-sha> for a merge commit
notes: Adds a new commit that undoes the old one. Safe on shared branches.

problem: Committed to the wrong branch (not pushed)
safest_fix: git branch <right-branch> && git reset --hard HEAD~1 && git switch <right-branch>
alternative: git switch <right-branch> && git cherry-pick <sha> then remove it from the wrong branch
notes: Check git status is clean first. If the right branch already exists use cherry-pick.

problem: Committed to main by mistake (already pushed)
safest_fix: git revert <sha> on main and cherry-pick <sha> onto a feature branch
alternative: Ask the team before any force-push to main
notes: Never force-push a shared default branch without agreement.

problem: Unstage a file
alternative: git reset HEAD <file> on old git
notes: Keeps the edits in the working tree.

problem: Discard local edits to one file
alternative: git stash push <file> to keep a copy
notes: The edits are gone for good unless stashed. Confirm first.

problem: Discard all local changes
safest_fix: git stash push -u -m "before discard" then git stash drop when sure
notes: clean -fd deletes untracked files with no recovery. Run git clean -nd first to preview.

problem: Recover a deleted branch
notes: Works while the commits are still in the reflog (about 90 days by default).

problem: Recover work lost after reset --hard
safest_fix: git reflog then git reset --hard <sha-before-reset> or git branch rescue <sha>
notes: Committed work is recoverable. Uncommitted work that was never staged is not.

problem: Recover a dropped stash
safest_fix: git fsck --unreachable | grep commit then git stash apply <sha>
notes: Only possible until git gc prunes it.

problem: Rebase went wrong while in progress
alternative: git rebase --skip for one bad commit
notes: Returns the branch to where it was before the rebase started.

problem: Rebase finished but the result is wrong
notes: ORIG_HEAD is overwritten by the next reset/merge/rebase so do this straight away.

problem: Merge conflict during merge
safest_fix: Fix the files then git add <files> && git commit
notes: Search for <<<<<<< markers before committing. Run the tests.

problem: Merge conflict during rebase
safest_fix: Fix the files then git add <files> && git rebase --continue
notes: Conflicts can repeat per commit. git rerere remembers resolutions.

problem: Undo a merge that is not pushed
notes: Check git log first: HEAD~1 is the first parent of the merge.

problem: Squash my last N commits before a PR (not shared)
safest_fix: git rebase -i HEAD~N and mark them squash or fixup
notes: Use git commit --fixup <sha> during work and git rebase -i --autosquash to fold them in.

problem: Split the last commit into smaller ones (not pushed)
safest_fix: git reset HEAD~1 then git add -p and commit each piece
alternative: git rebase -i and mark the commit edit
notes: Each new commit should build and pass tests on its own.

problem: Change an older commit (not pushed)
alternative: git rebase -i <sha>~1 and mark it edit
notes: Everything after that commit gets a new sha.

problem: Update my branch after main moved (my branch is private)
notes: Rebase keeps history linear. Merge if others share the branch.

problem: Update a shared feature branch after main moved
alternative: Agree with the team before rebasing a shared branch
notes: Merge doesn't rewrite anyone else's history.

problem: Push was rejected (non-fast-forward)
alternative: git fetch && git merge origin/<branch> then push
notes: Never answer a rejection with --force on a shared branch.

problem: Must overwrite my own remote branch after a rebase
notes: --force-with-lease refuses if someone else pushed in the meantime. Never use plain --force.

problem: Leaked a secret in a commit
safest_fix: Revoke or rotate the secret first then remove it in a new commit
alternative: git filter-repo --replace-text or BFG to purge history then force-push and have everyone re-clone
notes: Assume it is compromised the moment it was pushed. Purging history does not un-leak it. Check CI logs and forks too.

problem: Committed a large file by mistake (not pushed)
safest_fix: git rm --cached <file> && git commit --amend --no-edit then add it to .gitignore
notes: If it is pushed you need git filter-repo to shrink the repo.

problem: File should be ignored but is already tracked
safest_fix: git rm --cached <file> then add it to .gitignore and commit
notes: The file stays on disk. Other clones will delete it on pull.

problem: Detached HEAD with new commits
notes: Do this before switching away or the commits are only in the reflog.

problem: Bring one commit from another branch
alternative: git cherry-pick -x <sha> to record the source
notes: Prefer merging whole branches when you need many commits.

problem: Sync a fork with upstream
safest_fix: git fetch upstream && git rebase upstream/main
notes: Add the remote once with git remote add upstream <url>.

problem: Find which commit broke something
safest_fix: git bisect start then git bisect bad and git bisect good <sha>
notes: Finish with git bisect reset.

problem: Wrong author or email on recent commits (not pushed)
notes: Set git config user.email first.

problem: Remove a remote branch
alternative: Delete it in the hosting UI so it can be restored
notes: Check nobody has open work on it. Ask before running.
